target_customer: Pharma and biotech R&D teams, academic labs and computational biology groups that need to query, trace and govern research data
problem: Research data and models in biology are scattered across tools with poor lineage, versioning and governance, which limits reproducibility and AI work.
business_model: Open-source core (LaminDB, Apache-2.0 per a package listing) with a paid enterprise platform (LaminApp, support, schemas)
product_category: Open-source data lineage and lakehouse platform for R&D

founders.name: Alex Wolf
prior_employers: Cellarity (led the build-up of its compute platform)
founders.background_notes: Creator of Scanpy per the YC page and company about page; two decades of R&D software experience per the about page; education not listed.

founders.name: Sunny Sun
prior_employers: NYU (wet and dry lab genome engineering and cell biology work)
founders.background_notes: Per the company about page; degree details not listed.

founders.name: Frederic Enard
prior_employers: TF1 (4.5 years in enterprise data engineering)
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-CTO on the company about page; not listed as founder on the YC page, so treat the founder status as a company designation.

technical_complexity.rationale: A lineage-tracking, versioning and schema-validating data layer over SQL and object storage that must model biological data formats; standard engineering with domain hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Open-source adoption in computational biology through the Scanpy community creates trust and lock-in once data lineage is recorded; the code itself is open.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge in sources found; the company remains independent and describes itself as active in 2026.

market_need_then: The company says a big obstacle to better AI in R&D was a lack of a scalable way to query, trace and govern heterogeneous data; this comes from the company about page, not an independent source dated 2022.

branding.domain_note: Uses lamin.ai; acquisition details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific, 'git for R&D data' and 'by the creators of Scanpy'

branding.brand_signature: By the creators of Scanpy credential
branding.community_and_virality: Open-source Python package on PyPI and GitHub, with a skill for coding agents and a mention in a third-party Claude scientific skills collection per the company site.

brand_strength.rationale: Credibility comes from the Scanpy association and open-source use; the name is short but generic and shared with unrelated companies.

pivots.from: Git for R&D data: traceability and versioning with a biological data catalog
pivots.to: Open data platform for traceable, multimodal AI and agents
pivots.why: Company about page and PyPI descriptions show positioning shifting over time; no dated pivot source.

outcome_analysis: Lamin is active with about 12 people, offices in Munich and New York, and names pharma and academic users on its site. Funding is undisclosed on primary pages; backers listed include Y Combinator, Pillar VC, Dimension Capital and Pioneer Fund. The open-source core and Scanpy lineage give distribution in computational biology, while the paid platform and revenue are not independently verified.
notes: Funding unverified: Caplight 4.2M total with a seed in September 2022 (Y Combinator, Cherry Ventures), CB Insights 0.5M convertible note September 2022, Seedtable a 2025 seed with no amount (Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund, Pillar VC, Dimension Capital). Company about page lists investors but no amounts; no round recorded. A Pillar VC page returned 404. Competitor list is empty: searches for dated 2022 rivals found only LaminDB package listings; no source dated near the batch named an alternative, so this should be re-checked. Name origin not found. YC page lists two founders; the about page lists Sunny Sun as co-founder and President and Frederic Enard as co-CTO, so Enard is recorded per the company source.
